system: You predict physical quantities and explain your predictions. The picture attached to the task is a figure of a physics course. For each question, use the tool explain once: your prediction, an interval you are confident contains the true value, the unit, and the relation, from the candidates offered, that explains your prediction. An answer cannot be changed and you are not told whether it is right. When every question is answered, end with a short message that says, for each answer, whether it came from reading the picture or from the relation.
task:
The picture shows the velocity of that particle against time, simulated and exact. The particle has mass m = 0.5 kg, the drag constant is b = 0.25 kg/s, and g = 9.80665 m/s^2; it starts from rest and down is positive.

Answer every question with the tool explain.
1. Predict the terminal speed of the particle. Candidate relations: "v = m g / b"; "v = sqrt(m g / b)"; "v = b g / m"; "v = m g b".
2. Predict the time constant tau of the approach to the terminal speed: the time at which the velocity reaches 1 - 1/e of it. Candidate relations: "tau = m / b"; "tau = b / m"; "tau = m g / b"; "tau = sqrt(m / b)".
3. Predict the terminal speed if the mass were 1 kg, with the same drag constant. Candidate relations: "v = m g / b"; "v = sqrt(m g / b)"; "v = b g / m"; "v = m g b".
4. Predict the velocity of the particle 4 s after its release. Candidate relations: "v = (m g / b) (1 - exp(-b t / m))"; "v = g t"; "v = (m g / b) exp(-b t / m)"; "v = (m g / b) (1 - exp(-t))".

steps.text: Answering all four: the terminal speed and tau come from the relations (the picture agrees: the curve levels off near 19.6 m/s and reaches about 12.4 m/s at 2 s). Q3 comes from the relation only, since the picture is for 0.5 kg. Q4 uses the relation and agrees with the picture (about 17 m/s at 4 s).
